tasks.short: Work as one member of a firefighting crew

steps.what: Read the posted crew card for this firefighting assignment.
Collaborate with other firefighters as a crew member.

tasks.design: The incident commander posts a crew card on the {DOCS} with the unit, the role and the location. The firefighter reads that card, then crews the incident with the others. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet, and no machine assigns the role.
tasks.previous_blocker: The crew card was a paper list or a shout, and the assignment was not one posted line.
tasks.enabler_now: A posted card with unit, role and location can be opened on the {DOCS} the station already keeps.
tasks.still_hard: The firefighter still has to work the fire with the crew. A card does not see the smoke.
tasks.human_edge: Calling the next move on a hose line, an entry or a search is the crew's judgement in the moment.
tasks.altitude: Crewing the incident stays the week. The card is a shorter read, and the role is still the firefighter's to carry out.

reach.task: Post the crew card before arrival
reach.learn: The card names unit, role and location. It does not replace the crew.

evidence.claim: Annex III area 5(d) covers classifying emergency calls and dispatch priority, not crew work on the fire ground. This design does not rank roles or set a dispatch priority.
The next move on a hose line or a search is the crew's own judgement. This design adds no assignment score.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one incident, one crew, one firefighter. They crew the incident. They do not take the control-room call, write the incident archive, or set dispatch priority. The documents prior of 7.9 rounds to the crew-card read, share 8. The in-person prior of 86.8, plus the screen prior of 1.6, the mail prior of 3.6 and the sheet prior of 0.1, rounds to the crewing, share 92. Those scraps sit inside the crewing and are not a separate saving. No separate admin task is added.

Crew-card contract, produced by the incident commander before arrival, outside this task: unit id, role (hose, entry, pump, search) and location. No ranking of people and no risk score. The firefighter reads that card in {DOCS}, which is why the read drops to 75 percent; they still read it. If the card is blank the commander names the roles aloud and the read is not shorter. The commander's posting time is the commander's, not the firefighter's. Capture sits in the read. There is no machine step, no send, no alert, no sheet fill, and no step at zero remaining time.
Crewing itself is unchanged, so that step stays at 100 percent. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 is rechecking a stale crew card. The store running is not the firefighter's time.

tasks.short: Train new employees to control and suppress fires

steps.what: Read the posted lesson card on how to control fires.
Train new employees to control and suppress fires.

reach.task: Post the lesson card before the session

tasks.short: Assess the fire and report conditions by radio

steps.what: Read the posted alarm line before the radio call.
Assess fires and the situation before calling it in.
Report conditions to superiors on the two-way radios.
Receive instructions from superiors over those radios.

tasks.design: The control-room operator posts an alarm line on the {DOCS} with the address, the alarm class and the unit. The firefighter reads it, assesses the fire, reports conditions on the radio, and hears the order. Nothing sends the radio call, raises an alert, or fills a sheet, and no machine scores the fire.
tasks.previous_blocker: Address and alarm class were only in the first radio burst, easy to miss once.
tasks.enabler_now: The control room can post address, alarm class and unit on the {DOCS} before the crew speaks.
tasks.still_hard: What the fire is doing, and what to tell the superior, is still seen on scene.
tasks.human_edge: The radio report is the firefighter's own account. A model must not speak it.
tasks.altitude: Assessing the fire and the radio call stay the work. The alarm line is a shorter read, and the words on the radio stay the firefighter's.

reach.task: Post the alarm line before the crew speaks
reach.learn: The line is address, alarm class and unit. The on-scene assessment stays with the firefighter.

evidence.claim: Annex III area 5(d) covers classifying emergency calls and dispatch priority, not the officer's own assessment on scene. This design does not score the fire or set dispatch priority.

Victim injury details are health data under Article 9. This design does not write an injury field. The firefighter may say what they see on the radio, and that speech is not copied into a record here.
Voice or location logs that show crew performance need works council consent under article 27(l). This design does not add a voice log or a location trail. The radio call stays spoken.
What the fire is doing is the firefighter's own judgement on scene. This design adds no condition score and does not speak the report.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one call, one crew, one firefighter. They assess the fire, report conditions and hear the order. They do not classify the emergency call, set dispatch priority, or write the incident archive. The documents prior of 3.7 and the screen prior of 0.4 are the alarm-line read, share 4. Assessment takes 62. The report takes 22 and hearing the order takes 12, covering the rest of the in-person prior of 89.6 and the mail prior of 6.3. Those three steps stay at 100 percent. No separate admin task is added.

Alarm-line contract, produced by the control-room operator before the crew speaks, outside this task: address, alarm class and unit id. No priority score and no injury field. The firefighter reads that line in {DOCS}, which is why the read drops to 75 percent; they still read it. If the line is blank the operator speaks the address on the radio and the read is not shorter. The operator's posting time is the operator's, not the firefighter's. Capture sits in the read. There is no machine step, no send, no alert, no sheet fill, and no step at zero remaining time.

Assessing, reporting and hearing the order are unchanged, so those steps stay at 100 percent. The report is the firefighter speaking, not a filled sheet. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 is rechecking a stale alarm line. The store running is not the firefighter's time. Consent is longer because an address can identify a household, and injury speech must not be copied into this record.
